title: [DECISION] Symmetric-key-only restriction on ikm_fd enforces key chaining safety
description: src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c lines 1805-1812: ikm_fd validation checks that the KEY fd must have key_type == CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_SYMMETRIC (rejected with -EBADF otherwise). This enforces a clear security boundary: only symmetric keys (derived via DO_KDF) can be used as IKM sources for further KDF stages. Asymmetric keys (RSA, EC) cannot be used as IKM. This is non-obvious: an implementation might allow any KEY fd as ikm_fd. But the restriction is correct: asymmetric keys are already public (or partially public); using them as IKM would blur key separation. The check is explicit and immediate: if (ks->key_type != CRYPTO2DEV_KEY_SYMMETRIC ...) → -EBADF. This prevents a class of semantic errors where an asymmetric key is accidentally passed as IKM for a subsequent KDF stage.
